newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville limits Fri firm, peak power to 200 MW.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville limits Fri firm, peak power to 200 MW.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) limited its offer for sales of firm power between 1300 and 2100 PDT on Friday to 200 megawatts, BPA said Thursday.
No volume restrictions were placed on non-firm sales.

Otherwise, BPA's price offers for daily surplus power were unchanged from Wednesday at $17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) between 1300 and 2100 PDT, $14.50 for hours 0800-1200 and 2200-2300, and $13.00 for hours 0100-0700 and the hour ending 2400.

For Friday, Bonneville also continued to include Southwest buyers in its offer of displacement power during light-load hours at $9.00 per Mwh. The offer, which applies only to buyers willing to displace thermal generation with BPA's hydroelectric supplies, was until Wednesday available only in the Northwest.

Trade sources said regional power demand has weakened as temperatures cool off, and although power generation is plentiful, hydroelectric output volumes tend to taper off between now and the start of the next water year in October.
